papers.title: Calcium Plasma Implanted Titanium Surface with Hierarchical Microstructure for Improving the Bone Formation.
papers.abstract: Introducing hierarchical microstructure and bioactive trace elements simultaneously onto the surface of titanium implant is a very effective way to improve the osseointegration between bone and implant. In this work, hierarchical topography was prepared on Ti surface via acid etching and sandblasting (SLA) to form micropits and microcavities then underwent Ca plasma immersion ion implantation (Ca-PIII) process. The surface wettability and roughness did not change obviously before and after Ca-PIII process. The in vitro evaluations including cell adhesion, activity, alkaline phosphatase (ALP), osteogenic genes (Runx2, OSX, ALP, BSP, Col1a1, OPN, and OC), and protein (BSP, Col1a1, OPN, and OC) expressions revealed that the introduction of Ca ions onto the surface of SLA-treated Ti can promote greater osteoblasts adhesion, spread and proliferation, which in return further accelerated the maturation and mineralization of osteoblasts. More importantly, in vivo evaluations including Micro-CT evaluation, histological observations, push-out test, sequential fluorescent labeling and histological observations verified that Ca-SLA-treated Ti implants could efficiently promote new bone formation in early times. These promising results suggest that Ca-SLA-treated Ti has the potential for future application in orthopedic field.

summary_zh.motivation: 通过表面改性引入层次微结构和生物活性元素以增强骨整合。
summary_zh.method: 采用酸蚀喷砂和钙等离子体浸没离子注入处理钛表面。
summary_zh.result: 改性表面促进成骨细胞黏附、增殖和矿化，体内实验显示早期新骨形成。
summary_zh.validation: 通过体外细胞实验和体内植入实验（Micro-CT、组织学、推出试验）验证。

summary_en.motivation: To improve osseointegration of titanium implants by introducing hierarchical microstructure and bioactive calcium ions via surface modification.
summary_en.method: Titanium surfaces were treated with sandblasting and acid etching (SLA) followed by calcium plasma immersion ion implantation (Ca-PIII).
summary_en.result: Ca-SLA-treated Ti surfaces enhanced osteoblast adhesion, proliferation, and mineralization, and promoted early new bone formation in vivo.
summary_en.validation: In vitro cell assays and in vivo rat implant models with Micro-CT, histology, push-out tests, and fluorescent labeling.

papers.title: A 3D bioprinted complex structure for engineering the muscle–tendon unit
papers.abstract: Three-dimensional integrated organ printing (IOP) technology seeks to fabricate tissue constructs that can mimic the structural and functional properties of native tissues. This technology is particularly useful for complex tissues such as those in the musculoskeletal system, which possess regional differences in cell types and mechanical properties. Here, we present the use of our IOP system for the processing and deposition of four different components for the fabrication of a single integrated muscle-tendon unit (MTU) construct. Thermoplastic polyurethane (PU) was co-printed with C2C12 cell-laden hydrogel-based bioink for elasticity and muscle development on one side, while poly(ϵ-caprolactone) (PCL) was co-printed with NIH/3T3 cell-laden hydrogel-based bioink for stiffness and tendon development on the other. The final construct was elastic on the PU-C2C12 muscle side (E = 0.39 ± 0.05 MPa), stiff on the PCL-NIH/3T3 tendon side (E = 46.67 ± 2.67 MPa) and intermediate in the interface region (E = 1.03 ± 0.14 MPa). These constructs exhibited >80% cell viability at 1 and 7 d after printing, as well as initial tissue development and differentiation. This study demonstrates the versatility of the IOP system to create integrated tissue constructs with region-specific biological and mechanical characteristics for MTU engineering.

summary_zh.motivation: 构建具有区域特异性力学和生物特性的肌肉-肌腱组织。
summary_zh.method: 集成器官打印系统，共打印热塑性聚氨酯、聚己内酯和载细胞水凝胶生物墨水。
summary_zh.result: 成功制造了具有梯度力学性能和高细胞活力的肌肉-肌腱复合结构。
summary_zh.validation: 通过力学测试和细胞活性染色验证。

summary_en.motivation: To fabricate an integrated muscle-tendon construct with region-specific biological and mechanical properties.
summary_en.method: Used a multi-material 3D bioprinting system to co-print thermoplastic polyurethane, polycaprolactone, and cell-laden hydrogel bioinks.
summary_en.result: Successfully produced a construct with graded mechanical properties (elastic muscle side, stiff tendon side) and high cell viability.
summary_en.validation: Mechanical testing and cell viability assays at 1 and 7 days post-printing.
